title.en: Taiwan's Water Paradox: Too Much Rain, Not Enough Water

source.note: No workbook sheet exists for this SDG 6 mission; authored from scratch per docs/plans/new-mission-playbook.md.

narrative_brief: Taiwan gets 2.5 times the world's average rainfall but can use only a fifth of the world's average water per person. This talk traces that paradox from geography and typhoon dependency through the 2021 drought, reservoir sedimentation, diversification solutions, and the climate-driven squeeze between flood and drought risk.

stages.source_description: Part 1: Introduction (Slides 1-3: hook on the flood/drought contradiction, SDG 6 definition, Taiwan's rainfall-vs-usable-water paradox)

A2.text: Taiwan has a strange water problem. In some years, we must save every drop. In other years, heavy rain causes terrible floods. Why does this happen to us?
A2.authored_by: Claude + Gemini 3.1 Pro draft, fully rewritten by Claude for band compliance
A2.basis: New mission, no workbook source. Facts: Taiwan annual rainfall ~2,500mm, ~2.5x world average, but usable water per capita only ~4,074 m3/yr (~1/5 world average) (Water Resources Agency, MOEA). ~80% of rain falls May-Oct; typhoons + summer plum rains supply >50% of annual water; 2021 was the first year since 1964/56 years with no typhoon landfall, triggering the worst drought in decades (WRA; Earth.org; NPR/KPBS Apr 2023). Deji Reservoir sedimentation ~47% of capacity lost (WRA data, widely reported). 2021 drought: 17 of 19 major reservoirs <50%, Baoshan No.2 ~7%, Techi ~4.4%, rationing 2 days/week for >1 million households ~2 months (Earth.org; NPR). National reservoir dredging has exceeded average annual sediment inflow since 2022 (WRA); Shihmen Amuping Desilting Tunnel operating since Sept 2023 (WRA). Hsinchu desalination plant ~13,000 tonnes/day; national pipe leakage fell from ~20% a decade ago to ~14% now (Earth.org). Water price ~NT$11/tonne, several times cheaper than US/UK (Earth.org). Agriculture uses >70% of Taiwan's water but <2% of GDP (Earth.org; multiple sources). Register per docs/plans/new-mission-playbook.md.

A2.text: Taiwan needs fresh ideas for a drier future. Let's not just wait and hope for rain. Let's use our skills to build a smarter water system for everyone.
A2.authored_by: Claude + Gemini 3.1 Pro draft, fully rewritten by Claude for band compliance
A2.basis: New mission, no workbook source. Facts: Taiwan annual rainfall ~2,500mm, ~2.5x world average, but usable water per capita only ~4,074 m3/yr (~1/5 world average) (Water Resources Agency, MOEA). ~80% of rain falls May-Oct; typhoons + summer plum rains supply >50% of annual water; 2021 was the first year since 1964/56 years with no typhoon landfall, triggering the worst drought in decades (WRA; Earth.org; NPR/KPBS Apr 2023). Deji Reservoir sedimentation ~47% of capacity lost (WRA data, widely reported). 2021 drought: 17 of 19 major reservoirs <50%, Baoshan No.2 ~7%, Techi ~4.4%, rationing 2 days/week for >1 million households ~2 months (Earth.org; NPR). National reservoir dredging has exceeded average annual sediment inflow since 2022 (WRA); Shihmen Amuping Desilting Tunnel operating since Sept 2023 (WRA). Hsinchu desalination plant ~13,000 tonnes/day; national pipe leakage fell from ~20% a decade ago to ~14% now (Earth.org). Water price ~NT$11/tonne, several times cheaper than US/UK (Earth.org). Agriculture uses >70% of Taiwan's water but <2% of GDP (Earth.org; multiple sources). Register per docs/plans/new-mission-playbook.md.

B1.text: Taiwan needs fresh thinking for a drier future. Let's stop simply hoping the rain arrives on schedule, and let's start building a system that can handle whatever climate we get.
